findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment:
Observed the following food-contact surfaces that have an buildup of soil residues:
(i) the ice machine on the front panel and inside on the interior baffle.
(ii) the interior of the soda gun dispenser holder.
PIC was notified and will have these items cleaned. Ensure that food-contact surfaces are kept clean to sight and touch.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. [Pf]

findings.title: Toxic substances properly identified, stored and used.
findings.comment: Observed a working bottle of a chemical without a label. PIC stated that it was a sanitizer. CORRECTED: PIC contacted another PIC, and the chemical was confirmed to be a quaternary ammonium-based sanitizer. PIC labeled the bottle “SANITIZER”. Ensure that all working containers that are storing potentially toxic materials are labeled with the common name of the material to prevent misuse.
findings.citation_text: 7-102.11 Common Name. Working containers used for storing POISONOUS OR TOXIC MATERIALS such as cleaners and SANITIZERS taken from bulk supplies shall be clearly and individually identified with the common name of the material. [Pf]

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean.
findings.comment:
Observed the following nonfood-contact surfaces with an accumulation of soil residues:
(i) the underside of the coffee maker.
(ii) the interior edges of the mini freezer.
PIC was notified and will have these areas cleaned by the next routine inspection. Nonfood-contact surfaces of equipment should be cleaned with enough frequency to prevent an accumulation of soils.
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(C) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris. [C]

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment: Observed that the backsplash above the handwashing sink is not sealed to the counter, leaving a crevice that cannot be easily cleaned. Also observed the same backsplash was not sealed to the window sill, leaving a gap that cannot be easily cleaned. Floors, walls, and ceilings must be made smooth, and easily cleanable. PIC will seal these crevices to prevent the entry and harborage of mold and other soil residues.
findings.citation_text: 6-101.11(A)(1) Surface Characteristics. (A) Except as specified in (B) of this section, materials for indoor floor, wall, and ceiling surfaces under conditions of normal use shall be: (1) SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE for areas where FOOD ESTABLISHMENT operations are conducted. [C]

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
findings.comment: Inspector observed ice in the basin of the hand washing sink at the start of today’s inspection- indicating that it was being used as a dump sink. CORRECTED- the ice went down the drain as the inspector washed their hands. Ensure hand washing sinks are used for hand washing only, to incentivize hand washing.
findings.citation_text: 5-205.11 Using a Handwashing Sink. (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing. [Pf]

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment: FIRST REPEAT: Bare wood trim and walls were observed in the ice machine room. Floors, walls, and ceilings must be made smooth, and easily cleanable. Seal or paint bare wood to prevent the entry and harborage of mold.
findings.citation_text: 6-101.11(A)(1) Surface Characteristics. (A) Except as specified in (B) of this section, materials for indoor floor, wall, and ceiling surfaces under conditions of normal use shall be: (1) SMOOTH, durable, and EASILY CLEANABLE for areas where FOOD ESTABLISHMENT operations are conducted. [C]

findings.title: Management, food employee and conditional employee; knowledge, responsibilities and reporting
findings.comment:
There was no signed reporting agreement on file for the employee present during this inspection. CORRECTED- Employee reviewed and signed a blank reporting agreement from the orange binder. Ensure employees are educated on foodborne illnesses and symptoms that would exclude them from work around food. Keep signed reporting agreements on file for all food employees.
2-103.11: (O) FOOD EMPLOYEES are informed in verifiable manner of their responsibility to report accordance with LAW, to PIC, information about their health related to disease transmissible through FOOD. [C]

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
1) 1st REPEAT: Seal walls 2’ around the mop sink and 2’ above the faucet so that they are protected from water. 
2) Bare wood trim was observed in the ice machine room. Seal bare wood so it is smooth, easily cleanable, and nonabsorbent.
6-501.11: PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair. [C]

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
Mold buildup was observed in the ice machine bin on the ceiling behind the baffle and on the baffle along the lower edge. Owner will call for service to get the ice machine serviced and cleaned. 
4-601.11: (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. [Pf]

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
1) Bare wood shelf above the mop sink needs to be painted/sealed.
2) Seal walls 2’ around the mop sink and 2’ above the faucet so that they are protected from water. 
6-501.11: PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair. [C]

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.citation_text:
4-602.11 Ice machine was serviced since the routine inspection, and the ceiling inside the bin behind the baffle looked better. However, mold was still present in some spots. The baffle still had mold on the front surface behind the door hinge, and mold was also observed on the the back side near the ceiling. Owner plans to call for additional service. Ensure surfaces inside the bin are free from mold accumulation and maintained to minimize buildup. See general comments for additional information.
Equipment with enclosed components, such as ice machines, shall be cleaned at a frequency specified by the manufacturer, or absent manufacturer specifications, at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil or mold.

findings.title: Single-use/single-service articles: properly stored and used
findings.citation_text: 4-903.11 Violation remains to be corrected by next routine inspection. See 10/19/22 inspection report for details.

findings.title: Sewage and waste water properly disposed
findings.citation_text: 5-403.12 Violation remains to be corrected by next routine inspection. See 10/19/22 inspection report for details.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.citation_text:
5-205.11 Handwashing sink was used to dump and refill solution from a spray bottle. Proper use of handwashing sink was discussed. Middle basin at 3 part sink was emptied to allow for free flowing rinse and use of the basin for tasks unrelated to handwashing.
Handwashing sinks are to be accessible at all times and used only for handwashing.

findings.title: Food separated and protected
findings.citation_text:
3-304.11 Mold buildup was observed in the ice machine bin on the ceiling behind the baffle and on the baffle along the lower edge and along the door hinge. Owner will call for service to get the ice machine serviced and cleaned.
Food shall only contact equipment and utensils that are cleaned and sanitized as specified in Parts 4-6 and 4-7 of this Code; single-service and single-use articles; and linens, such as cloth napkins, as specified under § 3 304.13 that are laundered as specified under Part 4-8 of this Code.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.citation_text:
4-501.114 Quat solution prepared at bar 3 part sink was less than 200ppm. One tablet was used to make the solution. An additional tablet was added to bring the concentration right at 200ppm. Ensure enough tablets are used based on the amount of water in the sink to provide a sanitizer concentration at 200-4400pm as directed by label instructions for the product.
A quaternary ammonia compound solution shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions and be maintained at the concentration as indicated by the manufacturer's use directions included in the labeling.

findings.title: Single-use/single-service articles: properly stored and used
findings.citation_text:
4-903.11 1. Boxes with sleeves of 12oz and 16oz cups were on the floor in the women’s restroom shower room that is used for storage.
2. Package of paper towels was half on the floor in the designated storage location in the furnace room. Proper storage was discussed with owner. 
Single service articles shall be stored in a clean, dry location, where they are not exposed to splash, dust, or other contamination, and at least 6 inches above the floor.

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
findings.citation_text:
4-302.14 4-302.14 Quat test strips were not registering properly, and some of the strips appeared to have water damage with felt pads being a lighter color and/or not properly attached to the strip. Test strips in question were thought to be the same strips from the year prior, which were also not registering properly but did not appear to have water damage at the previous inspection. Provide new test strips and ensure storage that protects the test kit from potential water damage.
A test kit that accurately measures the concentration of sanitizing solutions in mg/L shall be provided.

findings.title: Sewage and waste water properly disposed
findings.citation_text:
5-403.12 Drain line from ice machine bin empties on the floor adjacent to the floor drain in the furnace room resulting in buildup of moisture and mold. Bin drain line needs to be re-directed to drain properly into the floor drain. 
Condensate drainage and other non-sewage liquids shall be drained from point of discharge to disposal according to law.

findings.title: All food employees have food handler training
findings.comment:
410 ILCS 625  Sec. 3.06 Copy of food handler certification was not available for the bartender working when inspector arrived on-site. Employee noted they have a certification, but it hasn’t been printed. Ensure copies of food handler certificiaotns are maintained on-site for all staff, including those that only help cover shifts periodically. 
All food handlers, other than someone who has the food service sanitation manager certificate, shall receive or obtain training in basic food handling principles as outlined in Subpart M of the Illinois Food Code.

findings.title: Management, food employee and conditional employee; knowledge, responsibilities and reporting
findings.citation_text:
2-103.11 (O) Employee health documents could not be located, and signed reporting agreements were not available for the owner or any of the staff. Employee health documents were provided and discussed. Owner and employee working at the time of inspection reviewed and signed copies of the reporting agreements. Owner was advised to ensure all staff are educated on the employee health policy and that new hires are educated upon hiring. Signed copies of reporting agreements need to be maintained on-site for staff that work at the bar and/or have potential to help at the bar.
The person in charge shall ensure that food employees are informed in a verifiable manner of their responsibility to report in accordance with law, to the person in charge, information about their health and activities as they relate to diseases that are transmissible through food, as specified under ¶ 2-201.11(A).

findings.title: Procedures for responding to vomiting and diarrheal events
findings.citation_text:
2-501.11 A cleanup procedure for responding to vomit/diarrhea incidents was not available. Norovirus disinfection policy was provided and discussed. Maintain the norovirus disinfection policy with employee health documents. 
A food establishment shall have written procedures for employees to follow when responding to vomiting or diarrheal events that involve the discharge of vomitus or fecal matter onto surfaces in the food establishment. The procedures shall address the specific actions employees must take to minimize the spread of contamination and the exposure of employees, consumers, food, and surfaces to vomitus or fecal matter.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.citation_text:
5-205.11 Ice was observed in the basin of the bar handwashing sink indicating it was used as a dump sink. Also, the employee working at the time of inspection started to empty chemical spray bottles at the handwashing sink. Employee was educated on proper use of the handwashing sink. Owner was advised to educate all staff on proper use of the handwashing sink.
Handwashing sinks are to be accessible at all times and used only for handwashing. Cease the practice of the handsink as dump sink.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.citation_text:
4-602.11 Mold accumulation was observed on the baffle in the ice machine. The majority of buildup was noted along the top behind the door hinge. Clean and sanitize inside the ice machine as frequently as needed to eliminate buildup of mold between full service cleanings.
Equipment with enclosed components, such as ice machines, shall be cleaned at a frequency specified by the manufacturer, or absent manufacturer specifications, at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil or mold.

findings.title: Toxic substances properly identified, stored, and used
findings.citation_text:
7-102.11 Spray bottles of pink liquid hanging at the bar 3 part sink were not labeled as to the contents. Bottles contained quat sanitizer and were labeled during the inspection. 
Working containers used for storing poisonous or toxic materials such as cleaners and sanitizers taken from bulk supplies and/or prepared on-site shall be clearly and individually identified with the common name of the material

findings.title: Toxic substances properly identified, stored, and used
findings.citation_text:
7-202.12 Quat solution in spray bottles was observed at a concentration above 400ppm. Test strips registered a color that was not on the comparison chart. Effective concentration for the product in use is 200ppm. Solutions were prepared using a mixture of 5oz of product in a spray bottle with water. The directions call for 1oz of product per gallon of water. Solutions were discarded and remade using appropriate measurements to obtain a concentration of 200ppm. Ensure all staff are educated on proper mixing of solutions, and use test strips to verify the concentration.
Chemical sanitizers must meet the concentration and use requirements specified by 40 CFR 180.940. Toxics shall be used according to the manufacturer's use directions included in labeling, and must not be used in a manner that poses a health hazard or potential risk of cross contamination.

findings.title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored
findings.citation_text:
3-304.14 Used wiping cloth was observed by spray bottles containing quat solution. Proper storage of wiping cloths between uses in sanitizer solution was discussed. If spray bottles are used, then wiping cloths are good for one use and must immediately be placed in the soiled linen storage or disposable paper towels should be used. 
Cloths in-use for wiping counters and other equipment surfaces shall be held between uses in a chemical sanitizer solution maintained at proper concentration for the sanitizer product being used.

findings.title: Single-use/single-service articles: properly stored and used
findings.citation_text:
4-903.11 Box with sleeves of 16oz cups was observed on the floor across from the ice machine. Proper storage was discussed with owner. 
Single service articles shall be stored in a clean, dry location, where they are not exposed to splash, dust, or other contamination, and at least 6 inches above the floor.

findings.title: Certified Food Protection Manager (CFPM)
findings.citation_text: 2-102.12 Owner has not completed the food manager certification. None of the employees on-site at the time of inspection had a food manager certification. Options for food manager courses to obtain CFM were discussed.  Person in charge at the time of inspection shall be a certified food manager.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.citation_text:
2-301.13 & 2-301.14 Bartender was observed wiping hands on a bar rag hanging between the 3 part sink and the trough used to ice down beer. Bartender was observed cleaning and sanitizing the soda gun holder at the 3 part sink prior to wiping hands. Inspector observed the same bar rag being used to wipe down beer bottles removed from the trough of ice. Employee was advised that common towels of any kind should not be used to wipe hands. If hands need to be wiped then they should be washed with proper technique and dried with disposable paper towels. 
Employees shall clean their hands and exposed portions of their arms immediately before engaging in food preparation including working with exposed food, clean equipment and utensils, and unwrapped single-service and single-use articles. Hands shall be washed between tasks and after engaging in activities that contaminate the hands.
Food employees shall properly wash their hands with the following procedure: (1) rinse under clean, running warm water; (2) apply soap; (3) rub together vigorously for at least 10 to 15 seconds; (4) thoroughly rinse under clean, running warm water; and (5) immediately follow the cleaning procedure with thorough drying. 
To avoid recontaminating hands, use a disposable paper towel or similar clean barrier when touching surfaces such as manually operated faucet handles on a handwashing sink.
Use only disposable paper towels for wiping hands.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.citation_text:
6-301.14 Handwashing signage was not posted at the bar handsink or in the restrooms. Handwashing signs were posted during the 2018 inspection but have been removed. Provide handwashing signs for all handsinks.
A sign or poster that notifies food employees to wash their hands shall be provided at all handwashing sinks used by food employees and shall be clearly visible to food employees. CORE

findings.title: Food obtained from approved source
findings.citation_text:
3-201.11  Portions of cooked and cooled foods that appeared to be items such as pulled pork and chili were observed in the pizza freezer. Owner stated said foods were brought in for a party and left to be picked up later. Persons saving said food never came back to get it. Items were discarded upon request of inspector.
Food shall be obtained from sources that comply with law. Leftover cooked and cooled foods are not allowed per the medium risk classification of the facility. Also, foods prepared in a private home kitchen should not be kept on-site for any reason, with the exception of small portions brought in for individual consumption by staff for lunch or dinner.

findings.title: Food in good condition, safe, and unadulterated
findings.citation_text: 3-101.11 Open bottle of peach juice in the walkin cooler had a best by date of May 3, 2019. The product was separated and discolored. Owner stated it was likely leftover from a party. Juice was discarded during inspection. Food shall be safe, unadulterated and honestly presented

findings.title: Food separated and protected
findings.comment:
3-302.11 Open can of pineapple juice was observed in the bottom of the bar reach-in cooler used for beverages and non-TCS condiment storage. Pineapple juice was removed and discarded. 
Food shall be protected from contamination by storing food in packages, covered containers, or wrappings.  Store unused portions of acidic juices in a clean, food grade containers for long term storage.
findings.citation_text:
3-305.11 Boxes containing syrups for beverage dispensing system were observed on the floor by the door to the walkin cooler. The floor was damp and had general buildup of debris. One box was broken, and the syrup sack was falling out and in contact with the floor. Store the boxes of drink syrups up off the floor.  
Food shall be protected from contamination by storing the food in a clean, dry location; where it is not exposed to splash, dust, or other contamination; and at least 6 inches above the floor.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-301.11 Sanitizer solution was not available at the bar for wiping surfaces during service. Spray bottle of 409 was the only product available. Bleach solution at 150ppm was provided for wiping surfaces. Maintain a sanitizer solution for wiping surfaces at the bar during hours of operation. Bleach needs to be maintained at 150ppm per product label directions and quat solution needs to be maintained at 200-400ppm per product label directions.
Chemical sanitizers shall be provided and available for use during all hours of operation.

4-501.114 Quat solution prepared at bar 3 part sink was less than 200ppm. Two tablets were used to make the solution. An additional tablet was added to bring the concentration to 200ppm. 
A quaternary ammonia compound solution shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions and be maintained at the concentration as indicated by the manufacturer's use directions included in the labeling. Maintain quat solutions at 200-400ppm as directed by the label instructions and use test strips to verify concentration.
findings.citation_text:
4-602.11 Mold accumulation was observed on the baffle in the ice machine and on the ceiling behind the baffle. Clean and sanitize inside the ice machine as frequently as needed to eliminate buildup of mold. 
Soda gun holder was soiled with buildup of mold and puddling liquid that was not draining properly. Drain line was cleaned (see #51), and the soda gun holder was cleaned and sanitized. 
Equipment with enclosed components, such as ice machines, and components of beverage dispensing equipment shall be cleaned at a frequency specified by the manufacturer, or absent manufacturer specifications, at a frequency necessary to preclude accumulation of soil or mold.

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures
findings.citation_text:
3-501.16 Foods in the walkin cooler had internal temperatures ranging from 46F-49F due to the walkin cooler not maintaining proper temperature (see #33). Some products were discarded (velveeta and salsa). Bottles of recently purchased juice were moved to the bar cooler that was observed at 39F-40F. 
Except during preparation or cooking cold time/temperature control for safety (TCS) foods shall be maintained at 41F/below.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition
findings.citation_text:
3-501.17 Open gallon of milk was observed without a date mark in the walkin cooler. Bartender thought it was brought in by someone for personal use. Milk was less than 1/3 full and discarded during inspection. 
Commercially processed, refrigerated, ready to eat TCS foods shall be clearly dated, at the time the original packaging is opened and if held for more than 24 hours, to indicate the date or day by which the food shall be consumed or discarded. The day the original container is opened is counted as day 1, and the date mark may not exceed a manufacturer’s use-by date if the manufacturer determined the use-by date based on food safety.

findings.title: Proper cooling methods used; adequate equipment for temperature control
findings.citation_text:
4-301.11 Walkin cooler was observed holding above 50F with infrared thermometer. Stem thermometers were placed in the cooler and confirmed a temperature of 50F-53F. TCS foods were removed from the cooler to be relocated or discarded depending on the product (See #22). Owner stated the cooler has been checked by two companies that stated the walkin is fine it just has issues maintaining temperature in extreme temperatures of cold or heat. Owner was advised the cooler must not be used for storage of any TCS foods if it is not going to be serviced and is unable to maintain cold TCS foods at 41F/below. Owner agreed to cease use of the walkin for storage of juice and other foods that require refrigeration. 
Equipment for cold holding shall be sufficient in number and capacity to maintain food at proper temperature.

findings.title: Thermometers provided & accurate
findings.citation_text:
4-204.112 &  4-302.12 Thermometer was not present in the walkin cooler. Also, a food thermometer was not available for checking temperatures. Thermometers were purchased at a local supply store and provided for use during inspection. 
Cold holding equipment used for TCS food shall be designed to include and shall be equipped with at least one permanently affixed temperature measuring device that is located to allow easy viewing of the device's  temperature display.
Food temperature measuring devices shall be provided and readily accessible for use in ensuring attainment and maintenance of food temperatures.

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
findings.citation_text:
4-302.14 Quat test kit was not available for checking sanitizer solution prepared using Steramine tablets used for ware washing. A test kit was purchased at a local supply store and provided for use during inspection.
A test kit that accurately measures the concentration of sanitizing solutions shall be provided.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.citation_text:
4-602.13 Walkin cooler shelving was soiled with black mold. Clean the shelving. 
Nonfood contact surfaces shall be cleaned at a frequency necessary to eliminate buildup of grease, food splash and general debris.

findings.title: Plumbing installed; proper backflow devices
findings.citation_text:
5-205.15 Drain hose to soda gun holder was clogged with mold buildup and not draining properly. Hose was cleaned during inspection to allow for proper drainage to help eliminate puddling liquid in the base of the soda gun holder.
A plumbing system, including fixtures such as drain hoses, shall be maintained in good repair and cleaned as often as needed to maintain them clean.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.citation_text:
6-501.12 Condenser, fan covers, and ceiling above the condenser were soiled with buildup in the walkin cooler. Clean the aforementioned items in the walkin cooler. 
Physical facilities shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean

findings.title: Adequate ventilation and lighting; designated areas used
findings.citation_text:
6-305.11 Personal food items were observed stored in coolers at the bar and in the walkin cooler intermixed with food for customers. Proper storage of personal items separate from food and beverage provided for customers was discussed. Provide a designated storage area for personal food items that does not bring in to question the purpose of said items.
Suitable facilities shall be provided for the orderly storage of employees' personal items.

findings.title: All food employees have food handler training
findings.comment: 410 ILCS 625  Sec. 3.06 Staff have not completed the online food handler certification. All staff that are not certified food managers need to complete an online food handler certification course that is ANSI and IL approved. Copies of certifications need to be maintained on-site.

findings.title: Potential for cross-contamination; storage practices; damaged food segregated
findings.citation_text:
750.120 - Soda gun, nozzle, and holder were observed with heavy mold accumulation, especially around the gun where the nozzle attaches and in the bottom of the holder. All items were cleaned and sanitized during the inspection.

Food and equipment shall be protected from cross contamination at all times. Clean and sanitize the soda gun and holder daily to eliminate buildup of mold.

findings.title: Thermometers, gauges, test kits provided
findings.comment:
750.830g - Quat test strips were observed to be damaged and not registering concentration properly. Test strips were discarded. Obtain and use a new set of quat test strips for checking the solutions prepared with sanitizer tablets (200ppm).

A test kit shall be provided and used for checking the concentration of chemical sanitizer that measures the concentration of solution in parts per million.

findings.title: Food contact surfaces of equipment and utensils clean
findings.comment:
(R) 750.800b - Mold buildup was observed inside the ice machine on the front upper part and backside of the baffle. Ceiling also had some mold accumulation around the opening where ice comes out. Owner was advised on cleaning and sanitizing in the ice machine.

Clean and sanitize in the ice machine at least weekly or more often if needed to eliminate buildup of mold.

findings.title: Sewage and waste water disposed properly
findings.citation_text:
750.1130 - The drain hose for the soda gun was clogged and not draining properly as a result of mold buildup in the holder (see #7b above). Drain hose was cleaned along with the holder to allow for proper drainage. Maintain the soda gun holder and drain hose clean to allow for proper drainage.

Bucket used for the soda gun drain hose was observed with mold accumulation. Bucket was removed for cleaning and replaced with a new container. Maintain the bucket clean and empty it daily.
 
Liquid waste shall be disposed of as sewage.

findings.title: Approved source
findings.citation_text:
750.100 - Ham and beans were provided by a customer who began the cooking process in his home kitchen. Home prepared foods are not allowed to be served to the public. Customer removed the food from the facility. (see general comments)

Food shall be obtained from sources that comply with all laws relating to food and food labeling.  The use of home prepared or home canned foods is strictly prohibited.

findings.title: Cold food at proper temperatures during storage, display, service, transport, and cold holding
findings.citation_text:
750.151 - Open package of turkey hotdogs and a half gallon of milk were observed in the walkin cooler. Staff were unsure as to when the items were opened, and the milk had a best by date of 11/15 on the carton. Foods in question were discarded.

Refrigerated, ready to eat foods that require time/temperature control for safety and are held at the establishment more than 24 hours shall be clearly dated and used or discarded w/in 7 days. Properly date mark food and do not hold longer than 7 days.

findings.title: Potential for cross-contamination; storage practices; damaged food segregated
findings.citation_text:
750.120 - Ice scoop was observed sitting on a box of garbage bags on top of the ice machine. Ice scoop was removed for cleaning. Store the scoop in a cleanable container (e.g. tupperware, etc.), and maintain the storage container and scoop clean.

Food and equipment shall be protected from potential cross contamination at all times.

findings.title: Hands washed, good hygienic practices (observed).
findings.citation_text:
750.510 & 1120 - Bartender was observed using a cloth towel for wiping hands. If hands need to be wiped, then they should be properly washed at the designated handsink. Handwashing was discussed.

Wiping cloths and common towels are prohibited. Cease the practice of using cloth towels for wiping hands. Employees shall properly wash their hands any time hands may have been contaminated and prior to handling food, clean equipment, and unwrapped single service articles.

findings.title: Food contact surfaces of equipment and utensils clean
findings.comment:
750.800b - The following food contact surfaces were soiled:
A) inside ice machine - lower left corner of metal baffle (mold);   and
B) soda gun holder (old fruit fly casings) - cleaned and sanitized during inspection. 

Properly clean and sanitize food contact surfaces between uses/as needed to prevent cross contamination and eliminate buildup of debris. In-use items, such as pizza cutter, etc. must be cleaned and sanitized up to every 4hrs after continuous use.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
750.800e - The following non-food contact surfaces were soiled:
A) drip tray of the bottom pizza (food debris);
B) shelves under pizza ovens (dust accumulation);  and
C) drain hose to soda gun (mold buildup) - cleaned during inspection.

Clean non-food contact surfaces daily/as needed to eliminate buildup of debris.

findings.title: Rooms clean, lockers provided and used, clean
findings.citation_text:
750.1280 - Jacket was observed on the counter between the handsink and the coffee maker. Store personal items away from service area.

Adequate area must be provided for the storage of employee belongings segregated from the food preparation and food storage area to reduce the potential for cross contamination.  Properly store all employee belongings.

findings.title: Food protection during storage, prepartion, display, service, transportation
findings.comment: 750-120(a) Observed the ice bin lid to be opened during the inspection. Facility was not busy and scooping of ice was not immediately occurring. Lid was closed. Food shall be protected at all times. Properly store and protect food.

findings.title: Hands washed, good hygienic practices (observed).
findings.comment: 750-1120e Observed a common towel at the handsink. Cease use of the common towel. The towel has a hook adjacent to the ice bin for storage. Remove hook to keep staff from using this common towel.   Hand-cleansing soap shall be available at each lavatory. Sanitary towels or a heated air hand-drying device shall be conveniently located near each lavatory. Common towels are prohibited. If disposable towels are provided a waste receptacle shall be conveniently located near the hand washing facilities.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces designed, constructed, maintained, installed, located.
